title: SmartStyler - Multi-Vendor Fashion Marketplace
description: SmartStyler is a full-stack, fashion-focused multivendor e-commerce marketplace built as my Final Year Project, and one of the most technically complex systems I've built during my university phase. It connects buyers, sellers, and platform administrators through three separate, independently deployed applications sharing one backend and database a real-world microservice-style separation of concerns rather than a single monolithic dashboard. The platform differentiates itself from a standard e-commerce clone through three research-driven features: TikTok-style reel-based product discovery, an ML-based "Find Similar Products" visual/semantic recommendation engine, and an integrated AI chatbot for customer support combined with real-time chat, Stripe payments, and a full seller-onboarding and dispute-resolution workflow.

detailSections.heading: Why we built it
detailSections.content: I built SmartStyler along with my friend as my final year thesis project to explore how modern discovery mechanics (short-form video, TikTok/Instagram Reels) and machine learning could be applied to solve a real problem in e-commerce static product grids are a poor way to discover fashion. I wanted the platform to feel like a social app first and a marketplace second, so I built reel-based browsing as the primary discovery surface, backed by a recommendation system that could actually understand product similarity, not just category tags. Beyond the buyer experience, I deliberately scoped this as a three-sided marketplace  sellers needed their own operational dashboard (inventory, analytics, order processing, disputes) and the platform needed independent administrative oversight (moderation, seller approval, dispute resolution) because that three-role complexity is what makes a marketplace a genuine systems-design problem rather than a CRUD app. The full thesis documents the system architecture, ML approach, and evaluation in detail.

detailSections.heading: Buyer Web App
detailSections.content:
Grid and Reel-based product browsing , alongside traditional filtered product listing/category browsing
ML-based "Find Similar Products" a dedicated recommendation engine to find similar products
AI chatbot embedded platform-wide for customer support
Real-time buyer and seller chat via WebSockets 
Google OAuth + JWT-based authentication, email verification, password reset
Full shopping flow cart, wishlist, checkout, Stripe payment processing with success/failure handling
Browsing history, store pages, liked reels, order tracking, support/dispute submission

detailSections.heading: Seller Central Dashboard
detailSections.content:
Full product CRUD with variant management (colors, sizes, etc.)
Reel upload - sellers create the short-form product videos that power the buyer discovery feed
Sales analytics dashboard
Order processing and fulfillment workflow
Real-time customer chat interface
Review management, billing, brand registration with OTP-based verification, and dispute/support handling

detailSections.heading: Admin Panel
detailSections.content:
Seller request approval/rejection workflow (marketplace gatekeeping)
Platform-wide product, category, and brand management
Reels moderation
Dispute resolution and support ticket handling
Admin role management with a separate secured admin-gateway login
Platform analytics overview and reviews moderation

detailSections.heading: Tech & Architecture
detailSections.content:
Frontend (all 3 apps): React 18 + Vite, Redux Toolkit for state management (with redux-persist on seller/admin), React Router v7, Tailwind CSS, React Hook Form + Yup for validated forms.
UI Libraries: Material UI (@mui/material, @mui/x-date-pickers) on seller and admin panels for data-dense dashboard UI custom Tailwind components on the buyer app for a lighter, consumer-facing feel.
Data Visualization: Recharts for seller/admin sales and platform analytics dashboards.
Real-Time Communication: Socket.IO client integrated into all three apps for live buyer↔seller and support chat.
Payments: Stripe.js integration on the buyer app for checkout, with dedicated success/failure redirect pages.
Authentication: JWT-based auth across all three apps, Google OAuth on the buyer side, OTP verification for seller brand registration, and a distinct gated login flow for the admin panel.
AI/ML Integration:
Chatling AI - embedded chatbot widget for customer support (loaded via script injection in index.html).
ML-based recommendation engine  a "Find Similar Products" feature calling a dedicated backend/ML endpoint that returns visually/semantically similar products across the marketplace, likely powered by a similarity model (deep-learning embeddings), covered in full in the thesis.
Backend (shared across all 3 frontends, per thesis/stack listing): Node.js + Express, MongoDB + Mongoose, with Cloudinary for media (product images/reels) storage.
DevOps: Netlify for hosting all three frontends independently; Render for backend hosting; CI/CD pipelines for automated deployment.
Architecture: A three-frontend, one-backend marketplace architecture  buyer, seller, and admin are fully separate React SPAs (independently built, deployed, and versioned) that all consume the same Express/MongoDB API, communicating in real time via Socket.IO and coordinating role-specific permissions (buyer, seller, admin) at the API layer.

title: QuickBgRemove - AI Background Remover & Image Editor
description: An AI-powered full-stack image processing application built for fast, high-quality background removal and seamless image editing. QuickBG combines AI background-removal models with image-processing capabilities to let users remove backgrounds in seconds, replace them with custom or generated backgrounds, resize images, and enhance image quality through an intuitive web interface.

detailSections.heading: Why i built it
detailSections.content: I built QuickBgRemove to solve a simple, recurring problem removing image backgrounds quickly without sacrificing quality or relying on paid or complex editing software. What started as an experiment with AI-based background removal evolved into a practical image editing tool that I and my family members actively use. I expanded the project beyond background removal by adding background replacement, AI-generated backgrounds, image resizing, Unsplash-powered background discovery, and image enhancement, turning it into a more complete image editing workflow.

detailSections.heading: What it does
detailSections.content:
AI Background Removal - Removes image backgrounds within seconds while maintaining high-quality subject edges.
Background Replacement - Replace removed backgrounds with custom images or discover backgrounds through the Unsplash API.
AI Background Generation - Generate new backgrounds to create completely different visual compositions.
Image Resizing - Resize processed images to custom dimensions.
Image Enhancement - Improve image quality using server-side Sharp processing.
Fast Image Processing - Handles AI inference and image transformations through a dedicated backend processing workflow.
Simple Editing Workflow - Upload, remove the background, customize the result, and export the edited image from one interface.

detailSections.heading: Tech & Architecture
detailSections.content:
Frontend: React + Tailwind CSS for a responsive image-editing interface.
Backend: Node.js API responsible for image processing, model integration, and application logic.
AI: Integrated Hugging Face models for AI-powered background removal and image generation capabilities.
Image Processing: Sharp for server-side resizing, optimization, format conversion, and image enhancement.
External API: Unsplash API integration for sourcing background images.
Architecture: Full-stack client/server architecture separating the interactive editing experience from AI inference and image-processing operations.
Processing Pipeline: Images are uploaded → processed through AI background removal → optionally transformed with a generated or selected background → resized/enhanced → prepared for final output.

title: SafarAI - AI Travel Itinerary Planner
description: An AI-powered full-stack travel planning app built with Next.js that turns a few trip preferences into a complete, day-by-day itinerary. SafarAI generates structured travel plans - destinations, daily activities, budget breakdowns, weather forecasts, and location images by combining an LLM-driven planning engine with several free public APIs for geocoding, weather, and imagery, all wrapped in a full authentication and trip-management system.

detailSections.heading: Why I Built It
detailSections.content: I built SafarAI to explore how far AI could go in automating something people usually spend hours on manually: planning a trip. Rather than just calling an LLM and returning raw text, I wanted the output to be a genuinely usable, structured itinerary complete with real coordinates, live weather, and destination images  so I designed a pipeline that combines AI generation with real-world data enrichment. It pushed me to work with authentication, database modeling, external API orchestration, and reliability patterns like model fallback, all within one cohesive product.

detailSections.heading: What It Does
detailSections.content:
AI Itinerary Generation — Users input destinations, dates, budget, trip type, pace, and interests; the app generates a full day-by-day itinerary with activities, timing, and estimated costs.
Multi-Model AI Fallback — Automatically tries a sequence of free LLMs via OpenRouter (Nemotron, Gemma, Qwen) until one returns a valid response, improving reliability without paid API dependency.
Location Enrichment — Automatically geocodes each destination and activity using OpenStreetMap/Nominatim to attach real coordinates.
Live Weather Forecasts — Pulls forecast data for each destination and day from Open-Meteo and attaches it directly to the itinerary.
Destination Imagery — Fetches relevant images for each location via the Wikipedia REST API.
Budget Breakdown — Splits the estimated budget across accommodation, food, transport, activities, and miscellaneous costs.
User Accounts & Trip Management — Full authentication (register, sign-in, email verification, password reset) with the ability to save, view, update, and delete trips tied to a user profile.
Robust AI Output Parsing — Custom JSON extraction logic handles messy or malformed LLM output (markdown fences, extra text, brace/array matching) to reliably parse structured itinerary data.

detailSections.heading: Tech & Architecture
detailSections.content:
Framework: Next.js 15 (App Router) with React 19 and TypeScript.
Styling/UI: Tailwind CSS v4 + Radix UI primitives (shadcn-style components) for accessible, composable UI.
Database: MongoDB with Mongoose for trip and user data modeling.
Auth: NextAuth.js with bcrypt password hashing, email verification, and password-reset flows (via Nodemailer).
AI Layer: OpenRouter API with a multi-model fallback chain (Nemotron, Gemma, Qwen free-tier models) for itinerary generation, plus custom JSON-extraction logic to robustly parse LLM output.
External APIs: Nominatim/OpenStreetMap for geocoding, Open-Meteo for weather, Wikipedia REST API for destination images — all free, no-API-key services chosen for cost efficiency and graceful fallback.
Architecture: Full-stack Next.js app with route-handler API endpoints (/api/trip/generate, /api/trip/get-trip, /api/auth/*, /api/profile/*) separating AI orchestration, data enrichment, and persistence layers.
Processing Pipeline: User submits trip preferences → input sanitized/validated → AI generates raw itinerary JSON → JSON parsed/repaired → activities enriched with geocoding, weather, and images → final itinerary persisted to MongoDB and returned to the client.

title: Wizbay
description: Wizbay is a large-scale multivendor e-commerce marketplace built by Elexoft for a client in Greece a complex, production system serving multiple sellers, brands, and product categories. This was the first project I worked on at Elexoft, where I contributed to both backend logic and UI/frontend changes on an existing, actively-developed platform rather than building it from scratch.

title: Conn-1
description:
Conn-1 is a scalable middleware platform built at Elexoft to integrate third-party fashion dropshipping APIs with WizBay, a multi-vendor marketplace.

The system imports, transforms, and publishes products from external suppliers and continuously keeps products, inventory, prices, variants, and other product data synchronized with WizBay.

We successfully scaled the platform to 150,000+ products on WizBay. Product imports and publishing jobs run every 3 hours, ensuring the marketplace stays regularly updated with the latest supplier data.

Conn-1 also handles order synchronization, product updates, availability changes, deletions, and other integration workflows between external providers and WizBay.

detailSections.heading: My Role In Conn1 Project
detailSections.content:
I led the Conn-1 project with a cross-functional team of five, including QA, UI/UX, and frontend developers.
Architecting the overall microservices system
Designing product and order synchronization workflows
Developing the backend services and API integrations
Implementing asynchronous processing using queues and background workers
Designing data mapping and transformation between supplier APIs and WizBay
Deploying and managing microservices on AWS/Kubernetes
Configuring HPA-based horizontal scaling
Supporting frontend development and API integration
Coordinating technical work across the development and QA teams

detailSections.heading: Why We Built Conn-1
detailSections.content:
WizBay was approaching launch, but the marketplace needed a larger product catalog and there were not yet enough sellers.

The client wanted to integrate fashion dropshipping APIs containing products from major brands such as Balenciaga, Gucci, and other premium brands.

Instead of tightly coupling these external APIs with WizBay, we built Conn-1 as a dedicated integration layer e.g Supplier APIs → Conn-1 → WizBay. This allowed us to automatically import and publish a large catalog while keeping product information synchronized every three hours. It also made it easier to support additional suppliers and integrations without changing the core WizBay marketplace.

detailSections.heading: Key Achievement
detailSections.content:
Successfully integrated and synchronized 150,000+ products with WizBay.
Automated product import and publishing every 3 hours, keeping the marketplace catalog continuously updated.
Designed the system to be capable of handling millions of products through distributed, queue-based processing.
Built the core synchronization workflow around background workers and asynchronous queues, allowing large-scale operations to run reliably without blocking the main application.
Deployed the architecture as scalable microservices on AWS/Kubernetes with HPA, enabling the system to scale with increasing workloads.
